metadata.description: Maintainer account compromise via phishing leading to trojanized npm packages with browser-targeted cryptocurrency wallet swap payload. Update vector (#10.1): existing packages receiving poisoned updates via permissive semver ranges.

path.description: Phishing email impersonating npm support, sent from typosquat domain npmjs.help. Claimed urgent 2FA credential update required. Maintainer (Qix) entered credentials on spoofed login page. Generic vulnerability: human psychological susceptibility — authority bias and artificial urgency.

dre.title: Credentials Harvested
dre.desc: Maintainer npm credentials captured by attacker phishing kit. Enabling cluster: #9.

path.evidence: Community disclosure by Josh Junon; npmjs.help domain registered 3 days prior to attack.

path.description: Attacker authenticates as Junon on the npm registry using stolen credentials. R-CRED: credential use is always #4 regardless of acquisition method.
Trojanized versions of 18+ packages (chalk, debug, and others) published via the legitimate npm publish API. The API works as designed; the maintainer's authority scope is abused.

dre.title: Package Integrity Compromised
dre.desc: 18+ npm packages published with trojanized code via legitimate publish API.

path.description: Trust Acceptance Event (Update Vector / #10.1). Consumers with permissive semver ranges (^x.y.z) pulled poisoned versions as routine updates. Consumers with pinned versions or lockfile enforcement were not affected.

Package manager resolves the updated version, downloads, and unpacks the content. The resolver honored the semver range; the installer processed the package. Controls: lockfile-enforced version pinning, registry allowlists, install sandboxing.
Malicious JavaScript executes when the consuming application runs in a browser. The payload operates exclusively in browser environments. R-EXEC: FEC execution via designed mechanism.

Payload hooks browser APIs (window.ethereum, fetch, XMLHttpRequest) and uses Levenshtein distance algorithms to replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses across six blockchains. 280+ hardcoded fallback addresses. APIs function as designed; scope is abused.

dre.title: Crypto Wallet Swap
dre.desc: Transaction data intercepted (LoC) and wallet addresses modified in transit (LoI) across six blockchains.

bizRisk.title: Financial Loss — Cryptocurrency Theft
bizRisk.desc: Users' cryptocurrency transactions redirected to attacker wallets. Direct financial loss to end users of consuming applications.

path.evidence: Sonatype payload analysis; 280+ hardcoded wallet addresses across 6 blockchains.
